fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are copied into the stack-allocated lexer.inbuffer array (MAX_PACKET_LENGTH*2+1 = 18433 bytes); Size is up to 9216.
Each input byte is consumed sequentially by the packet state machine; inbuflen = inbufptr - inbuffer grows as bytes are processed.
A 0xd3 byte in GROUND_STATE transitions the lexer into RTCM3_LEADER_1, beginning RTCM3 packet recognition.
The byte following 0xd3 must have its top 6 bits zero; its low 2 bits become the high bits of the RTCM3 length.
The third byte supplies the low 8 bits of the RTCM3 length; length+3 payload bytes are then consumed before RTCM3_RECOGNIZED.
After the declared payload length is exhausted, the lexer enters RTCM3_RECOGNIZED.

fine_trace.code: for (idx = 0; idx < inbuflen; idx++) { if (0xd3 == lexer->inbuffer[idx]) { break; } }
fine_trace.note: The code scans the entire inbuffer for the first 0xd3 byte; idx is the position of that first 0xd3, which may be an earlier byte that was consumed as part of a different protocol, not the RTCM3 leader.

data_len is read from the two bytes following the first 0xd3 in the buffer. If that 0xd3 was not the RTCM3 leader, these bytes are unconstrained attacker data, so data_len can be up to 0xFFFF = 65535.

crc24q_check reads data_len+6 bytes starting at &inbuffer[idx]. With data_len up to 65535 and idx up to 9215, the read extends to index 9215+65541 = 74756, far beyond the 18433-byte inbuffer, causing a stack-buffer-overflow READ.
